World Health Day Observed at MGIMS; Joint Secretary GOI Reviews Key Health Initiatives
Wednesday, 08 April 2026
1257 Hits
Mahatma Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences (MGIMS), Sevagram, observed World Health Day today with a special program aligned with this year’s theme, ‘Together for Health: Stand with Science’.
The program was graced by Shri Elangbam Robert Singh, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Government of India, who is on a two-day visit to MGIMS, Sevagram. As part of his visit, he is reviewing hospital services, community health work, and the ongoing Swachhata Pakhwada activities. Other dignitaries present included Dr. BS Garg, (Secretary, Kasturba Health Society), Dr. AK Shukla (Dean, MGIMS), Dr Poonam Shivkumar (Medical Superintendent), Dr Ramesh Pandey (Adl Medical Superintendent) along with head of departments, consultants, residents, staff, students, and nurses.
In his address as the Chief Guest, Shri E Robert Singh emphasized the importance of reaching out to the common person. He appreciated MGIMS’s strong community connect and its efforts in translating research into impactful field-level interventions. Speaking at the occasion, he reaffirmed, “True impact lies not merely in systems, but in the emotion, commitment, and devotion that drive them. When we begin to think beyond ourselves and our families, we can genuinely work towards making this world a better place to live.”
Dr AK Shukla welcomed everyone and highlighted MGIMS’s commitment to providing accessible, affordable, and community-oriented healthcare. “We aim to showcase MGIMS’s research journey aligning institutional efforts with national research priorities while addressing local health needs”, said Dr Subod Gupta (Head of Community Medicine) introducing the theme of the program.
Departments of MGIMS presented their research contributions, innovations that have been adopted by the Government of India or the Government of Maharashtra. Dr Arjun Jakasania showcased Department of Community Medicine’s work on CLICS (Community-Led Initiatives for Child Survival) —a women-led, decentralised healthcare delivery model that has strengthened grassroots health systems. The session also featured a panel discussion with community workers, including ASHA workers, sharing firsthand experiences of how villages have benefitted with improved maternal and child health outcomes due to MGIMS driven initiatives.
Dr Poonam Shivkumar presented the Department of Gynaecology’s immense contribution in policy making and in the management of Postpartum Haemorrhage (PPH), in reducing maternal mortality. Dr Vijayashree Khairkar showcased the Department of Microbiology’s  contributions in the prevention of  tuberculosis, zoonotic diseases, and hospital infection control, reflecting the One Health approach.
Dr Indrajeet Khandekar highlighted the Department of Forensic Medicine’s contribution in strengthening medico-legal practices, rationalising unnecessary post-mortems and improvising medical curriculum. Dr Anupama Gupta highlighted the Department of Pathology’s work on cancer registry, contributing to better disease surveillance and policy planning.
“The World Health Organization’s theme this year strongly resonates with MGIMS’s longstanding commitment to community-oriented, evidence-based healthcare,” said Dr. BS Garg.
